name: Gâteau Opéra
description: Six alternating layers of coffee-soaked joconde almond sponge, espresso buttercream, and bittersweet chocolate ganache, assembled flush and finished with a mirror-dark chocolate glaze — the apex of French patisserie elegance.

ingredients.note: Simple syrup (equal sugar and water, cooled)

name: Oysters with Mignonette Granita
description: French raw oysters served on crushed ice with a mignonette granita — shallot and sherry vinegar frozen into sharp, icy crystals that melt over the cold oyster, heightening the brine without masking it. The simplest luxury in the kitchen.

ingredients.note: Live oysters (Fines de Claire, Belon, or Kumamoto)

name: Oysters Rockefeller
description: Plump raw oysters baked on their half-shell under a blanket of creamed spinach, Pernod, and golden breadcrumbs — the grand New Orleans appetizer of 1899, as rich as its namesake.

ingredients.note: Fresh oysters on the half-shell, shucked (cup side up)
Shallots and garlic, finely minced together
Panko breadcrumbs and finely grated Parmesan, mixed 2:1

name: Oysters Rockefeller (gluten-free)
description: Plump raw oysters baked on their half-shell under a blanket of creamed spinach, Pernod, and golden breadcrumbs — the grand New Orleans appetizer of 1899, as rich as its namesake. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs.

ingredients.note: Fresh oysters on the half-shell, shucked (cup side up)
Shallots and garlic, finely minced together
instead of Panko breadcrumbs and finely grated Parmesan, mixed 2:1

name: Pad See Ew
description: Wide flat rice noodles stir-fried at ferocious wok heat with egg, Chinese broccoli, and sweet soy sauce until lightly charred — a dish that lives or dies by the 'wok hei' smoky breath of the fire.

ingredients.note: Fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai, 2-3 cm wide)
Chicken breast or thigh (thin sliced) or firm tofu
Gai lan (Chinese broccoli, cut in 5 cm lengths)
Kecap manis or dark sweet soy sauce
Neutral oil (high smoke point — canola or grapeseed)

name: Pad See Ew (gluten-free)
description: Wide flat rice noodles stir-fried at ferocious wok heat with egg, Chinese broccoli, and gluten-free sweet soy sauce until lightly charred — a dish that lives or dies by the 'wok hei' smoky breath of the fire. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free sweet soy sauce instead of kecap manis (sweet soy sauce), oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai, 2-3 cm wide)
Chicken breast or thigh (thin sliced) or firm tofu
Gai lan (Chinese broccoli, cut in 5 cm lengths)
instead of Kecap manis or dark sweet soy sauce
Neutral oil (high smoke point — canola or grapeseed)

name: Pain Perdu
description: Day-old brioche slices soaked in a vanilla-custard egg batter and cooked in foaming butter until the exterior forms a golden crust and the interior trembles like a warm custard — the original French toast.

name: Palak Dal
description: Toor dal cooked to a thick, golden-yellow soup, then folded with a puree of fresh spinach that colors it a deep forest green, finished with a mustard-seed, curry leaf, and asafoetida tadka that crackles and blooms across the surface like a spice-storm in miniature. Nutritionally dense and deeply comforting, this is the everyday dal that makes the subcontinent's protein work taste like a celebration.

name: Palak Dal (gluten-free)
description: Toor dal cooked to a thick, golden-yellow soup, then folded with a puree of fresh spinach that colors it a deep forest green, finished with a mustard-seed, curry leaf, and asafoetida tadka that crackles and blooms across the surface like a spice-storm in miniature. Nutritionally dense and deeply comforting, this is the everyday dal that makes the subcontinent's protein work taste like a celebration. This gluten-free version uses asafoetida (gluten-free) instead of asafoetida.

name: Pan-Seared Salmon
description: A single fillet, skin side down, given the patience it deserves — the skin shatters like glass, the flesh stays rose-pink at the center, and the boundary between the two is where all the magic lives.

name: Paneer Tikka
description: Cubes of firm paneer and jewel-bright peppers, thickly coated in a spiced yogurt marinade and blistered under high heat until the exterior chars and crackles while the inside stays milky and yielding.

ingredients.note: Red and green bell pepper, cubed
Fresh coriander and lemon wedges, to serve

name: Paneer (Fresh Indian Cheese)
description: Whole milk curdled at the precise moment with lemon juice, drained through muslin, and pressed under weight into a firm, yielding block of fresh white cheese — mild, clean, and with a characteristic squeak against the teeth. The foundational protein of Indian vegetarian cooking, made in 90 minutes from two ingredients.

ingredients.note: Whole milk (at least 3.5% fat — do not use UHT)
Fine sea salt (optional, worked in before pressing)

name: Panna Cotta
description: Piedmont's 'cooked cream' at its purest — cream barely warmed with vanilla and just enough gelatin to hold a trembling, barely-there set that quivers when the plate is nudged and collapses on the tongue into a cool wash of sweet milk.

ingredients.note: Crème fraîche or plain yogurt (optional, off-heat)

name: Paris-Brest
description: A wheel of golden choux pastry split open to reveal a cloud of hazelnut praline mousseline — light and airy where the pastry is crisp, rich and caramel-sweet where the cream hides. Named for a bicycle race, it tastes like the finish line.

name: Paris-Brest (gluten- & nut-free)
description: A wheel of golden choux pastry split open to reveal a cloud of sunflower seed praline mousseline — light and airy where the pastry is crisp, rich and caramel-sweet where the cream hides. Named for a bicycle race, it tastes like the finish line. This gluten- & nut-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, sunflower seeds instead of hazelnuts.

name: Pasta alla Carbonara
description: Rome's most demanding pasta — spaghetti cloaked in a trembling, egg-yolk-rich sauce that exists in the razor-thin margin between silky cream and scrambled catastrophe, punctuated by shards of crisped guanciale and a snowfall of aged Pecorino.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek), cut into lardons
Pasta cooking water, starchy and salted

name: Pasta alla Carbonara (gluten-free)
description: Rome's most demanding pasta — spaghetti cloaked in a trembling, egg-yolk-rich sauce that exists in the razor-thin margin between silky cream and scrambled catastrophe, punctuated by shards of crisped guanciale and a snowfall of aged Pecorino. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free spaghetti instead of spaghetti.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek), cut into lardons
Pasta cooking water, starchy and salted

name: Pasta e Fagioli
description: Naples's definitive cold-weather dish — short pasta and creamy white beans in a thick, rosetinted broth that hovers perfectly between soup and stew, built slowly on a soffritto base and finished with enough olive oil that each bowl shimmers.

ingredients.note: Dried borlotti or cannellini beans, soaked overnight
Short pasta: ditalini, tubettini, or broken spaghetti
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish

name: Pasta e Fagioli (gluten-free)
description: Naples's definitive cold-weather dish — short pasta and creamy white beans in a thick, rosetinted broth that hovers perfectly between soup and stew, built slowly on a soffritto base and finished with enough olive oil that each bowl shimmers. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta, gluten-free spaghetti instead of spaghetti.

ingredients.note: Dried borlotti or cannellini beans, soaked overnight
instead of Short pasta: ditalini, tubettini, or broken spaghetti
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish

name: Pastéis de Nata (Portuguese Custard Tarts)
description: Conceived by Jerónimo monks in Lisbon, these tarts exist at the intersection of violence and delicacy — shatteringly flaky pastry shells holding a barely-set custard that emerges from an inferno of an oven speckled with dark leopard spots of caramelized sugar.

ingredients.note: Lemon zest strip and cinnamon stick

name: Pastéis de Nata (Portuguese Custard Tarts) (gluten-free)
description: Conceived by Jerónimo monks in Lisbon, these tarts exist at the intersection of violence and delicacy — shatteringly flaky pastry shells holding a barely-set custard that emerges from an inferno of an oven speckled with dark leopard spots of caramelized sugar. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Lemon zest strip and cinnamon stick

name: Patina de Piris
description: A pear custard from the kitchens of imperial Rome, transcribed in Apicius — orchard pears pounded smooth with honey and a startling lick of black pepper, bound with eggs and a splash of fish sauce, then baked into a trembling, savoury-sweet flan that sets like a soufflé and slumps softly under the spoon.

ingredients.note: Garum / liquamen (fish sauce, a few drops)

name: Peach Melba
description: Escoffier's tribute to a soprano — ripe peaches poached whole in vanilla syrup until they slip from their skins, set over a quenelle of cold vanilla ice cream, and veiled in a raw raspberry melba sauce that bleeds crimson down the sides of the coupe.

name: Peach Melba (nut-free)
description: Escoffier's tribute to a soprano — ripe peaches poached whole in vanilla syrup until they slip from their skins, set over a quenelle of cold vanilla ice cream, and veiled in a raw raspberry melba sauce that bleeds crimson down the sides of the coupe. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

name: Pear Ginger Crisp
description: Juicy pears baked down into a honeyed, gently spiced filling with a double hit of ginger — warm fresh root and chewy candied bits — under a buttery, crunchy oat topping.

name: Pear Ginger Crisp (gluten-free)
description: Juicy pears baked down into a honeyed, gently spiced filling with a double hit of ginger — warm fresh root and chewy candied bits — under a buttery, crunchy oat topping. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free oats instead of porridge oats.

name: Pecan Pie Filling
description: A deep amber, caramel-scented custard bound with corn syrup and whole eggs, poured over toasted pecans that rise to the surface and lacquer to a glossy, crackle-topped crown.

name: Peking Duck
description: The pinnacle of Chinese roast cookery — a whole duck air-dried over 24 hours, lacquered with maltose and soy until the skin shatters at a touch, the fat rendered completely away beneath a burnished mahogany shell.

name: Peking Duck (gluten-free)
description: The pinnacle of Chinese roast cookery — a whole duck air-dried over 24 hours, lacquered with maltose and soy until the skin shatters at a touch, the fat rendered completely away beneath a burnished mahogany shell. This gluten-free version uses dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

name: Peperonata
description: Sweet bell peppers, onion, and tomato slow-braised in a generous pool of olive oil until every strip has completely collapsed into a silky, jammy compote that tastes more concentrated and sweet than anything a raw pepper ever promised.

ingredients.note: Mixed sweet bell peppers (red, yellow, orange — halved, seeded, cut into 1cm strips)

name: Peri-Peri Chicken
description: A whole spatchcocked chicken marinated in a ferocious sauce of African bird's eye chilies, garlic, lemon, and smoked paprika — then grilled low and slow until the skin is lacquered and blistered and every bite delivers heat that builds from the back of the throat forward.

name: Pernil (Puerto Rican Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder)
description: A bone-in pork shoulder buried in garlic-sazón adobo and marinated for 24 hours, then roasted low and slow until the meat is fall-apart tender — then blasted high to transform the thick skin into the crunchy, shattering cuerito that is the most coveted part of the entire dish.

ingredients.note: Bone-in pork shoulder (picnic or Boston butt), skin-on
Fresh cilantro with stems, roughly chopped

name: Persian Rice with Tahdig
description: Long-grain basmati steamed with saffron over a scorching base until a golden, burnished crust forms on the bottom — the tahdig that every Iranian competes to claim.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil or clarified butter (for pot)

name: Persian Chelo Rice with Tahdig
description: The crown jewel of the Iranian table — long-grain basmati parboiled, drained, and steam-finished over a shield of butter and potato that becomes the tahdig: an impossibly crisp, golden-amber crust that is the most fought-over piece on any Persian platter.

ingredients.note: Fine sea salt (for soaking and parboiling)

name: Persian Saffron Rice (Chelow)
description: The crown jewel of Iranian cooking — long-grain basmati that has been soaked, parboiled, and then steamed over a low flame wrapped in a cloth to create a golden, shatteringly crisp crust called tahdig at the bottom of the pot while the rice above remains separate, elongated, and perfumed with saffron.

ingredients.note: Saffron threads, bloomed in 3 tbsp hot water
Gluten-free flatbread gluten-free bread or gluten-free flatbread (optional tahdig base)

name: Persian Tahdig (Crispy Rice)
description: Rice that is as much about its golden, shattering crust as the fluffy grains above it — parboiled, rested, steamed under a towel-wrapped lid for an hour until the bottom transforms into a burnished disk that comes away from the pot in one dramatic, crackling sheet.

name: Peruvian Ceviche with Leche de Tigre
description: Thin-sliced sea bass cured in punishing lime juice and ají amarillo until the flesh turns white and tender, served in its own milky tiger's milk that you are expected to drink at the end.

ingredients.note: Fresh cilantro, leaves and thin stems
Choclo corn kernels (or corn on the cob)

name: Picarones
description: Peru's beloved fried doughnuts — rings of sweet potato and butternut squash dough, yeast-risen and crisp on the outside, pillowy within, drizzled with chancaca syrup spiced with anise and cinnamon.

ingredients.note: Orange-flesh sweet potato, cooked and mashed
Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Chancaca (raw cane sugar block) or dark muscovado sugar

name: Butter Pilaf
description: The pillar of Central Asian and Turkish cooking — long-grain rice toasted in butter until translucent and nutty, then steamed in stock with onion and carrot until each grain is firm, separate, and fragrantly golden.

ingredients.note: Chicken or lamb stock (hot); made up to 450 ml with boiling water

name: Polenta
description: Coarse cornmeal stirred into a slow whirlpool until the grains burst, swell, and pull away from the pot in a single glossy mass — patient, golden, and finished with a knot of butter and a storm of cheese.

name: Pollo a la Brasa (Peruvian Rotisserie Chicken)
description: A whole chicken brined in soy sauce, cumin, aji panca, and garlic for 24 hours, then roasted on a rotisserie or in the oven until the skin is burnished and crackled and the meat inside is so juicy and aromatic it needs nothing beyond the bright green aji verde served alongside.

ingredients.note: Garlic cloves, minced to a paste
Aji panca paste (or dried aji panca, rehydrated)
Fresh jalapeño or aji amarillo (for aji verde)

name: Pollo a la Brasa (Peruvian Rotisserie Chicken) (gluten-free)
description: A whole chicken brined in tamari, cumin, aji panca, and garlic for 24 hours, then roasted on a rotisserie or in the oven until the skin is burnished and crackled and the meat inside is so juicy and aromatic it needs nothing beyond the bright green aji verde served alongside. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Garlic cloves, minced to a paste
Aji panca paste (or dried aji panca, rehydrated)
Fresh jalapeño or aji amarillo (for aji verde)

name: Pollo en Adobo
description: Bone-in chicken braised in a deep brick-red Mexican adobo — ancho and guajillo chiles toasted, rehydrated, and blended with vinegar, garlic, cumin, and oregano into a glossy, chile-thick sauce that clings to the meat like varnish.

ingredients.note: Dried ancho chiles (stems and seeds removed)
Dried guajillo chiles (stems and seeds removed)
Chicken stock; made up to 300 ml with boiling water

name: Porchetta
description: A whole pork belly rolled around a core of fennel pollen, wild fennel fronds, rosemary, and garlic, then slow-roasted for hours until the fat renders completely and the skin transforms into a thunderous, blistered crackling that shatters into a thousand shards at the first cut. Central Italy's greatest street food, sliced and eaten in a gluten-free bread roll.

ingredients.note: Skin-on pork belly, deboned, butterflied flat
Fresh fennel fronds or wild fennel
Fennel seeds, toasted and coarsely ground

name: Chashu Pork Belly
description: A rolled pork belly tied tight, seared golden, and braised in soy, mirin, sake, and sugar until the fat is trembling and translucent — the canonical ramen topping.

name: Chashu Pork Belly (gluten-free)
description: A rolled pork belly tied tight, seared golden, and braised in soy, mirin, sake, and sugar until the fat is trembling and translucent — the canonical gluten-free ramen topping. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

name: Pork Belly Confit
description: Skin-on pork belly cured overnight in salt and aromatics, then slow-cooked submerged in its own rendered fat until the collagen surrenders completely — pressed flat overnight and finished with a skin so crisp it shatters like a pane of amber glass.

ingredients.note: Rendered pork fat or duck fat; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Pork Carnitas
description: Michoacán's definitive taco filling — pork shoulder braised slowly in its own rendered lard with orange, cinnamon, bay, and garlic until meltingly tender, then fried in that same fat until the edges shatter into mahogany-brown crackle while the center stays irresistibly juicy.

ingredients.note: Orange (1 large — halved, juice squeezed, shells reserved)
Mexican cinnamon stick (canela, one small piece)

name: Seared Pork Chops with Apples, Cabbage and Mustard Pan Sauce
description: Thick pork chops seared to a deep golden crust and rested until blushing and juicy, served over tart apples and cabbage softened in the pork fat and a tangy cider-mustard pan sauce glossed with butter.

ingredients.note: Bone-in pork rib chops, about 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick
Firm, tart-sweet apples (such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady), cored and cut into 1 cm wedges
Green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 100 ml with boiling water

name: Pan-Seared Roasted Pork Tenderloin
description: The most forgiving of the lean cuts — seared in a searing hot pan until mahogany on all sides, finished in a hot oven, then rested until the juices redistribute into a blush-pink, impossibly tender centre.

name: Pot-au-Feu
description: The most French of dishes — beef shin and marrow bones simmered slowly with root vegetables until the broth is golden and clear, served in two courses: broth first, then meat and vegetables.

ingredients.note: Marrow bones (5–6 cm sections, tied in muslin)
Large yellow onion (halved, cut-side charred dry in a pan)
Dijon mustard, cornichons, fleur de sel, and gluten-free bread (to serve)

name: Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
description: A well-marbled chuck roast seared dark and braised low in red wine and stock until it yields to a spoon, surrounded by carrots, parsnips, and potatoes that drink up the deep, beefy gravy.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck roast, boneless (about 1.6 kg), tied
Yellow onions, cut into thick wedges
Beef or chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Pot Roast with Root Vegetables (gluten-free)
description: A well-marbled chuck roast seared dark and braised low in red wine and stock until it yields to a spoon, surrounded by carrots, parsnips, and potatoes that drink up the deep, beefy gravy. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of worcestershire sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck roast, boneless (about 1.6 kg), tied
Yellow onions, cut into thick wedges
Beef or chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Chocolate Pots de Crème
description: Individual baked chocolate custards — richer than crème brûlée, darker in the cup, with a wobble that yields to a spoon like velvet. Barely set, barely sweet, deeply bitter, the coffee amplifying the chocolate's darkest notes.

ingredients.note: Espresso or very strong brewed coffee

name: Classic Prawn Bisque
description: A velvety coral-colored soup built from roasted prawn shells flambéed with cognac, simmered with mirepoix and tomato into a concentrated crustacean essence, then finished with cream until it flows like silk — rich, deeply saline, and perfumed with the sea.

ingredients.note: Whole raw prawns, peeled (flesh reserved for garnish)
Fine sea salt and white pepper

name: Kerala Prawn Curry
description: The coast of Kerala in a pot — whole prawns tumbled into a vivid, fiery coconut milk gravy built on mustard seeds, curry leaves, ginger, and chilli, cooked in under 15 minutes to keep the prawns tender and the coconut milk bright.

ingredients.note: Kukum puli (Malabar tamarind) or tamarind paste

name: Prawn Laksa
description: A bowl of rice noodles drowned in a broth that is simultaneously fiery, rich, and sour — the coconut cream folding around lemongrass and shrimp paste like a warm tide, plump prawns barely cooked in the final simmer.

ingredients.note: Large prawns, peeled and deveined (shells reserved)
Bean sprouts, laksa leaves (Vietnamese coriander), and sliced red chili

name: Prawn Saganaki
description: Plump prawns baked in a bubbling tomato and ouzo sauce, buried under a slab of crumbled feta that softens without melting, its saltiness pulling all the sweet tomato and briny prawn together into something irresistible. A Greek taverna dish made for a chunk of gluten-free bread and a glass of cold white wine.

ingredients.note: Raw shell-on prawns, head-on if possible (16/20 ct)
Feta cheese, crumbled into large chunks
Canned whole San Marzano tomatoes, hand-crushed
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Profiteroles with Chocolate Sauce
description: Airy choux puffs, hollow at the centre, filled with billowing vanilla chantilly and drowned under a silky warm chocolate sauce — the unreasonably perfect Parisian bistro dessert, made from nothing more than flour, butter, eggs, and chocolate.

name: Profiteroles with Chocolate Sauce (gluten-free)
description: Airy choux puffs, hollow at the centre, filled with billowing vanilla chantilly and drowned under a silky warm chocolate sauce — the unreasonably perfect Parisian bistro dessert, made from nothing more than gluten-free flour, butter, eggs, and chocolate. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Provençal Tian
description: Rounds of zucchini, ripe tomato, and waxy potato arranged in overlapping spirals in an olive-oil-slicked earthenware dish, then baked until every edge catches colour and the vegetables melt into each other at their touching faces.

ingredients.note: Ripe plum tomatoes, sliced 5 mm rounds
Waxy potato, peeled, sliced 5 mm rounds
Fresh thyme and rosemary, stripped from stems
Flaky sea salt and black pepper

name: Pulled Pork Shoulder
description: A pork shoulder rubbed with spices, smoked low and slow for hours until the bark is mahogany and the interior pulls apart in long, silky, juicy threads with zero effort.

ingredients.note: Hardwood chunks (oak, hickory, or apple wood)

name: Puls
description: The porridge that fed an empire — cracked emmer wheat coaxed in salted water until it surrenders into a thick, nutty pottage, glossed with oil and crowned with sharp cheese and herbs. This is the legionary's bowl, older than bread in the Roman kitchen and the bedrock of the Mediterranean table.

ingredients.note: Emmer wheat / farro (whole or coarsely cracked)
Fresh lovage or celery leaf, chopped

name: Puls (gluten-free)
description: The porridge that fed an empire — cracked emmer brown rice coaxed in salted water until it surrenders into a thick, nutty pottage, glossed with oil and crowned with sharp cheese and herbs. This is the legionary's bowl, older than gluten-free bread in the Roman kitchen and the bedrock of the Mediterranean table. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

ingredients.note: instead of Emmer wheat / farro (whole or coarsely cracked)
Fresh lovage or celery leaf, chopped

name: Pumpkin Pie
description: A silky, trembling custard of pumpkin and warm spice set in a buttery, shatteringly crisp crust — the pie that makes an entire holiday smell like cinnamon and brown sugar from the moment it goes into the oven.

ingredients.note: Pumpkin pie spice (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, clove, allspice)

name: Pumpkin Pie (gluten-free)
description: A silky, trembling custard of pumpkin and warm spice set in a buttery, shatteringly crisp crust — the pie that makes an entire holiday smell like cinnamon and brown sugar from the moment it goes into the oven. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pastry instead of shortcrust pastry.

ingredients.note: instead of 9-inch pie shell, par-baked (homemade or store-bought)
Pumpkin pie spice (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, clove, allspice)

name: Quinoa Tabbouleh
description: A gluten-free riff on the Levantine herb salad — cooked quinoa standing in for quinoa, but the spirit kept luminously intact: mostly flat-leaf parsley and fresh mint, punctuated by sweet tomato and cool cucumber, all dressed generously in sharp lemon and grassy olive oil.

ingredients.note: Persian or English cucumber, finely diced

name: New Orleans Red Beans and Rice
description: Creamy red kidney beans slow-simmered with Andouille sausage, the holy trinity, and a tangle of Creole seasonings — the Monday ritual of New Orleans, a dish of extraordinary comfort from the humblest pantry.

ingredients.note: Dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight

name: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
description: Thick slabs of pork belly melt through three hours of slow braising in Shaoxing wine and dark soy until the fat turns translucent and the skin lacquers to a deep mahogany that shimmers like polished rosewood. The sauce reduces to a trembling glaze that coats each piece in concentrated sweetness undercut by star anise and the ghost of fermented wine.

ingredients.note: Skin-on pork belly, cut into 4 cm cubes

name: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou) (gluten-free)
description: Thick slabs of pork belly melt through three hours of slow braising in Shaoxing wine and dark soy until the fat turns translucent and the skin lacquers to a deep mahogany that shimmers like polished rosewood. The sauce reduces to a trembling glaze that coats each piece in concentrated sweetness undercut by star anise and the ghost of fermented wine. This gluten-free version uses dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of dark soy sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Skin-on pork belly, cut into 4 cm cubes

name: Refried Black Beans
description: Frijoles refritos from the Oaxacan kitchen — black beans simmered until they surrender, then mashed into rendered lard with onion until they form a velvety, savory paste that holds a spoon upright.

ingredients.note: White onion (quartered for broth, diced for frying)

name: Beef Rendang
description: The Minangkabau's extraordinary dry beef curry — chunks of beef slow-cooked for hours in coconut milk with a complex paste of galangal, lemongrass, and chili until all liquid evaporates and the meat fries in its own released fat, coating itself in a dark, nearly black, intensely concentrated spice crust.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck or short rib, cut into 5 cm chunks
Lemongrass stalks, bruised and tied in a knot
Dried red chilies, soaked in hot water
Fresh turmeric, peeled, or 1 tsp ground turmeric

name: Ribollita
description: A thick Tuscan peasant soup built from the bones of yesterday's bread and the season's darkest cavolo nero — re-boiled until the beans dissolve into the broth and the torn bread swells to a trembling, almost porridge-like consistency that a spoon stands up in.

ingredients.note: Stale Tuscan pane sciocco (unsalted bread), torn
Cavolo nero (lacinato kale), stems removed, roughly chopped
Canned whole San Marzano tomatoes, hand-crushed
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Ribollita (gluten-free)
description: A thick Tuscan peasant soup built from the bones of yesterday's gluten-free bread and the season's darkest cavolo nero — re-boiled until the beans dissolve into the broth and the torn gluten-free bread swells to a trembling, almost porridge-like consistency that a spoon stands up in. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: instead of Stale Tuscan pane sciocco (unsalted bread), torn
Cavolo nero (lacinato kale), stems removed, roughly chopped
Canned whole San Marzano tomatoes, hand-crushed
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Rillettes de Porc
description: Pork shoulder cooked for hours in its own melting fat until every fiber surrenders, then shredded by hand and packed into crocks with enough fat to preserve it. Spread thickly on cold gluten-free bread, it is the most honest thing in the French charcuterie tradition.

ingredients.note: Lard or pork fat; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Quatre épices (white pepper, nutmeg, ginger, clove)

name: Risotto alla Parmigiana
description: The Milanese discipline of coaxing starch from rice — ladle by ladle, stir by stir — until each grain suspends in a creamy wave that flows like lava when the plate is tapped.

ingredients.note: Light chicken or vegetable stock (warm); made up to 800 ml with boiling water

name: Roast Chicken
description: The test of a cook, according to every French chef who ever lived — a whole bird, salt, butter, heat, and the nerve to leave it alone while the oven does its work.

name: Roast Pork Loin with Fennel and Apples
description: A fennel-and-garlic-rubbed pork loin roasted on a bed of apples, fennel, and red onion that slump into jammy sweetness, all brought together with a quick cider-mustard pan sauce.

ingredients.note: Pork loin roast, boneless, fat cap on (about 1.4 kg)
Fennel bulbs, trimmed and cut into 8 wedges each

name: Roasted Beet Salad with Goat Cheese and Walnut Vinaigrette
description: Deeply sweet roasted beets in multiple colors, warm from the oven and blushing after peeling, set over peppery arugula with crumbled goat cheese and dressed with a walnut-sherry vinaigrette that bridges the earthy and the bright. The beets roasted in their skins come out sweeter and more concentrated than any other method.

ingredients.note: Mixed beets — red, golden, and Chioggia (candy cane)
Arugula or mixed greens, washed and dried

name: Roasted Beet Salad with Goat Cheese and Pumpkin seeds Vinaigrette (nut-free)
description: Deeply sweet roasted beets in multiple colors, warm from the oven and blushing after peeling, set over peppery arugula with crumbled goat cheese and dressed with a pumpkin seeds-sherry vinaigrette that bridges the earthy and the bright. The beets roasted in their skins come out sweeter and more concentrated than any other method. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

ingredients.note: Mixed beets — red, golden, and Chioggia (candy cane)
Arugula or mixed greens, washed and dried

name: Salt-Crust Roasted Beets
description: Whole beets buried in coarse salt and roasted low and slow until the salt draws moisture and the beet's natural sugars concentrate into an intense, jewel-bright sweetness — a technique that takes far longer than foil-roasting but produces a flavor that is categorically different.

ingredients.note: Coarse sea salt or rock salt
Red wine vinegar or balsamic, for serving

name: Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini Lentils
description: Cumin-and-paprika cauliflower roasted until the edges char sweet and nutty, piled over earthy lentils dressed in a lemony, garlicky tahini. Warm, creamy, and bright with a heap of fresh parsley.

name: Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini Lentils (nut-free)
description: Cumin-and-paprika cauliflower roasted until the edges char sweet and nutty, piled over earthy lentils dressed in a lemony, garlicky tahini. Warm, creamy, and bright with a heap of fresh parsley. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

name: Whole Roasted Cauliflower
description: A whole head braised tender in salted, lemony water, then bronzed in the oven under a coat of olive oil until the curds turn nutty-sweet and the crown crisps into shattering, caramelized florets — served as a centerpiece, carved at the table like a roast.

ingredients.note: Whole cauliflower head (leaves trimmed, stem cut flat)
Flaky sea salt and black pepper (to finish)

name: Whole Roasted Cauliflower (nut-free)
description: A whole head braised tender in salted, lemony water, then bronzed in the oven under a coat of olive oil until the curds turn nutty-sweet and the crown crisps into shattering, caramelized florets — served as a centerpiece, carved at the table like a roast. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: Whole cauliflower head (leaves trimmed, stem cut flat)
Flaky sea salt and black pepper (to finish)

name: Roasted Root Vegetables
description: Parsnips, carrots, and beetroot — peeled and cut to size, tossed in a generous coat of oil, and roasted at high heat until their sugars have caramelized to a deep, bittersweet char — the most honest and satisfying way to eat the vegetables of an English autumn.

ingredients.note: Fresh thyme sprigs and bay leaves
Flaky sea salt and black pepper

name: Roasted Tomato & Garlic Soup
description: Tomatoes, onion, and a whole head of garlic roasted until blistered and caramel-edged, then blended into a thick, brick-red soup that tastes of late summer, with basil and a swirl of cream.

ingredients.note: Yellow onions, cut into thick wedges
Red bell pepper, seeded and quartered
Vegetable stock; made up to 750 ml with boiling water

name: Rum Baba
description: Tiny enriched yeast cakes soaked in warm rum syrup until fully saturated and dripping — Italian in origin, Parisian in execution, best crowned with Chantilly and a cherry.

ingredients.note: Vanilla pod or 1 tsp vanilla extract

name: Saag Aloo
description: Waxy potatoes tumbling in a vivid, spice-bloomed spinach sauce — mustard seeds pop, cumin follows, and the potatoes drink up every drop of green.

ingredients.note: Waxy potatoes (Desiree or Charlotte), cut into 3 cm cubes

name: Saag Paneer
description: Blanched spinach blended into a velvet-dark puree, simmered with ginger, garlic, and a bloom of whole spices until it becomes a rich, deeply savory sauce, then folded with golden-edged cubes of fresh paneer that hold their form against the silky green. The finished dish tastes like the forest floor and the hearth at the same time.

name: Chelow ba Tahdig
description: Persian saffron rice — the parboil-and-steam technique that produces rice of extraordinary refinement, each grain separate and impossibly light, perfumed with bloomed saffron, and crowned with a golden, shattering tahdig crust that the cook claims as their prize.

ingredients.note: Fine salt (for soaking and parboiling water)

name: Salt and Pepper Shrimp
description: Cantonese wok-fried whole shell-on shrimp that arrive at the table crackling and fragrant — the shells fried to a shattering crunch you eat whole, the flesh beneath barely cooked and sweet, buried under a confetti of garlic, scallion, and white pepper.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil, for wok-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Fresh red chillies, thinly sliced (optional but traditional)

name: Salt and Pepper Squid
description: Rings and tentacles tossed in spiced potato starch and flash-fried until the coating shatters at first bite — finished in the wok with garlic, chili, and spring onion that perfume the crust without softening it.

ingredients.note: Fresh squid tubes and tentacles, cleaned
Neutral oil for deep-frying (sunflower); for frying (only some is absorbed)
Long red chili and green chili, thinly sliced

name: Salt-Baked Branzino
description: A whole branzino buried in a thick egg-white salt crust and baked — the mineral shell seals in steam and moisture, cooking the fish impossibly gently within its own aromatics.

ingredients.note: Whole branzino (European sea bass), gutted and scaled

name: Salt-Baked Sea Bass
description: A whole sea bass encased in an egg-white-bound salt crust and baked until the crust sets hard as stone — inside, the fish has steamed in its own juices and the heat of the sealed crust, emerging perfectly cooked, sweet-fleshed, and explosively fragrant with ginger and scallion.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled (about 700g)
Coarse sea salt (not fine — it must be granular)
Scallions (spring onions), tied in a loose knot

name: Salt-Baked Sea Bass (gluten-free)
description: A whole sea bass encased in an egg-white-bound salt crust and baked until the crust sets hard as stone — inside, the fish has steamed in its own juices and the heat of the sealed crust, emerging perfectly cooked, sweet-fleshed, and explosively fragrant with ginger and scallion. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled (about 700g)
Coarse sea salt (not fine — it must be granular)
Scallions (spring onions), tied in a loose knot

name: Brandade de Morue
description: Provençal salt cod pounded or blended with olive oil and warm milk until it becomes a smooth, ivory emulsion — dense, luxurious, faintly fishy in the best possible way. Spread on crostini or gratinéed in a baking dish, it is the taste of the Languedoc coast in winter.

ingredients.note: Whole milk, warmed to hand temperature

name: Salt-Crusted Whole Fish
description: A whole fish sealed inside two kilos of egg-white-bound salt and baked until the crust rings like plaster — cracked at the table with a mallet, releasing a cloud of herbed steam and the most perfectly seasoned, juicy fish imaginable.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bass or sea bream (600-800 g), gutted and scaled

name: Saltimbocca alla Romana
description: Veal escalopes blanketed with prosciutto and sage, sautéed in butter until the ham crackles and the white wine pan sauce clings to every fold.

ingredients.note: Veal escalopes (noce or fesa), 150 g each

name: Samosa Filling
description: Fluffy mashed potato and sweet green peas coarsely folded with a crackling bloom of cumin, coriander seed, ginger, and green chili — the filling that has made samosas irresistible for centuries, fragrant and slightly drier than you expect so it holds its shape inside the crisp gluten-free pastry shell without steaming it soft. Every bite releases warm spiced starch and a bright herbal finish.

ingredients.note: Waxy potatoes (Yukon Gold or similar), boiled whole and peeled
Green peas (fresh shelled or frozen, thawed)
Green chilies (serrano or Thai), finely minced
Fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, finely chopped
